newsitem.title: USA: NYH spot heat oil holds strength on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: NYH spot heat oil holds strength on tight supplies.

text.p: New York Harbor (NYH) spot No. 2 oil differentials remained firm during early Friday activity, supported by tightness in prompt supplies and the cold snap in the U.S. Northeast.
On the NYMEX, May heating oil was up 0.55 cent while May gasoline was up 0.60 cent.
No. 2 oil sellers in NYH held their ground, and traders reported prompt barrels changing hands at 4.00 cents over the print, the upper end of the range created earlier this week.
However, prompt NYH low sulphur diesel diffs dipped modestly to between 4.50 and 4.75 cents over the NYMEX, down about 0.25 cent from Thursday.
NYH premium D4 gasoline diffs strengthened further, with prompt barrels talked between 6.00 and 6.50 cents over the print, up nearly 1.00 cent on the day and 2.00 cents from earlier this week.

U.S. Gulf conventional M1 gasoline for delivery on the back 12th cycle of the Colonial Pipeline was talked between about 2.50 and 2.60 cents under the print, up about 0.15 cent from late Thursday levels.
